name: watch.registry
description: Subscribe to registry-key changes. Emits EVENT frames per change until cancelled. Unlike registry.wait (one-shot), this verb fires on every change.

watch_subtree.description: If true, fire on changes anywhere in the key's subtree. Without this, only direct changes to `path` itself trigger.

x-event-schema.description: EVENT frames emitted per registry change. Win32 RegNotifyChangeKeyValue does NOT identify which value changed — the EVENT is a coarse `something in this key changed` signal; consumers re-read the key to see what changed.

path.description: The registry key that changed (echoes the input `path`; useful when multiple watch.registry subscriptions are active on the same connection).

x-implementations.name: reg_notify_change_key_value_loop
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegNotifyChangeKeyValue` in a loop on a dedicated thread — the API is one-shot (signals, must be re-armed). Each signal fires an EVENT and re-arms; loop exits on watch.cancel.

windows-modern.description: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue with REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_NAME | LAST_SET | ATTRIBUTES | SECURITY classes. Re-armed in a loop after each signal.

windows-classic.description: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue available since NT 3.1. Win 9x has limited registry-change support; classic agent on 9x falls back to a polling read loop.
